measure_type: % of collected US vaccine-related tweets and retweets that carried a link to a domain on a fake-news/unreliable-source list
value_raw: 26,998 fake-news-related tweets out of 'nearly four million geotagged tweets as well as the retweets'; 26,998/4,000,000 = 0.68%. The percentage itself is never printed and the exact corpus size is never printed.
denominator: Nearly four million geotagged US English tweets AND retweets matching COVID-19 vaccine keywords, 19 Apr-30 Jun 2021 (the exact N is never printed; the paper reports a mean of 79,894 geotagged tweets per state, which over 51 states implies about 4.07 million). The denominator includes the large majority of tweets that carry no URL at all, since untagged and URL-free tweets were classed 'others'.
definition: A tweet (original, retweet or quote) containing a URL whose domain name appeared on the Columbia Journalism Review list of 1,125 domains tagged fake, conspiracy, bias or unreliable; the tweet's own text was never judged for truth
misinfo_def: if the URL's domain name was judged on the basis of the opinion of communications scholar to be related to the websites containing fake news, conspiracy theories, unreliable contents, or extremely biased news, the tweets that were associated with (i.e., contained/retweeted/quoted) this URL were classified as fake-news-related
source_quote: Using the aforementioned URL-based tweet classification method, we detected 26,998 fake-news-related (fake news, conspiracy theories, unreliable contents, or extremely biased news) and 456,061 fact-related tweets.
page_loc: Results, section 3, p. 3; denominator from Methods section 2.1.1, p. 2
ground_truth_detail: Columbia Journalism Review list of 1,125 unique domains, built by merging the curated fake-news site lists of PolitiFact, FactCheck, OpenSources and Snopes; the authors kept the domains tagged fake, conspiracy, bias and unreliable. No tweet was itself truth-coded; the only manual work was a 100-tweet-per-class check that tweeters endorsed rather than debunked the linked content. No inter-rater statistic.
moderator_quote: Nearly four million geotagged tweets as well as the retweets posted from April 19, 2021, to June 30, 2021, were collected. The average number of geotagged tweets per state is 79,894 (Min = 2,796, Max = 715,871, and SD = 119,637).
notes: OVERRULED THE SCREEN ON CONSTRUCT: filed as CONTENT, coded here as SHARING (sharing_subtype content_share). The denominator is a keyword-collected stream of tweets AND retweets, i.e. what users chose to post and repost, classified by the domain of the link they carried, with no item-level truth judgement. Under the denominator rule that is behaviour-filtered content, and the re-extraction campaign already ruled the identical shape (a planetary-scale COVID tweet corpus classified by domain) SHARING rather than CONTENT. SOURCE-LEVEL, recorded as such: this is the share of tweets carrying a link to a flagged DOMAIN, not the share of tweets that were false. TWO THINGS A HUMAN MUST DECIDE. (1) R8: the 0.68% is not printed anywhere and the denominator appears only as the verbal 'nearly four million', so the value is a computation over an approximate denominator; applied strictly, R8 would drop this row. It is recorded here because the numerator is exact and the shape of the estimate is clear, but it should not be treated as a printed value. (2) Addendum D: the flagged group is a disjunction, 'fake news, conspiracy theories, unreliable contents, or extremely biased news', and the paper defines the last branch as sources that 'come from a particular point of view and may rely on propaganda, decontextualized information, and opinions distorted as facts'. That is hyperpartisan, which addendum D treats as different from unreliable, so the numerator is broader than the review's construct. breadth left empty because the classification is source-level.
